headline: Sox Suffer Ninth Inning Heartbreak To Complete Depressing Toronto Sweep
morning_brew: I watched the ninth inning of yesterday's game through my fingers, and it was just pure heartbreak. We had a chance to salvage something against Toronto, but instead, we serve up a four to three loss to complete a depressing three-game sweep. Sonny Gray did everything he could, giving up three runs over seven strong innings, but our offense gave him almost nothing to work with. Then, after a misplayed foul pop, Aroldis Chapman serves up a go-ahead double to Brandon Valenzuela with two outs in the ninth to seal our fate. What a devastating way to drop a ballgame.

We only managed five hits all afternoon, which is just not going to get the job done in the big leagues. This team is now twenty-nine and forty-three, sitting in a massive hole, and the frustration is reaching a boiling point. My neighbor Rick is already composing a letter to the commissioner over how that ninth inning went down, and honestly, I might help him mail it. You can't make mistakes like that when you're already struggling to score runs, and it feels like every single bounce is going against us right now.

While the baseball team heads out west to Seattle, we got some legendary news on the hockey front. The Bruins announced they are retiring Patrice Bergeron's number thirty-seven next season, which is just a class move for a true Boston legend who gave everything to this city. Down in Foxborough, the Patriots have officially completed their spring sessions. Drake Maye and the squad have a long summer of preparation ahead, and the front office better be on the phone right now to find some offensive line help before training camp kicks off.
